docs.text: Starting - A go-signal from RES is used to indicate the approval to begin. Timing starts after the vehicle crosses the starting line.

docs.title: D6.3.7
docs.text: After the run, the vehicle must come to a full stop within 30m behind the finish line on the track and enter the finish-state described in T14.9.

docs.title: D6.4.1
docs.text: 5 points are awarded to every team that finishes at least one run without DNF or DQ.

docs.title: D6.4.2
docs.text:
If a team’s corrected elapsed time is below Tmax, points based on the following formula are given:

[ \textit{AUTOCROSS SCORE} = 95\left(\frac{\frac{T_{max}}{T_{team}} - 1}{\frac{T_{max}}{T_{min}} - 1}\right) ]

  • Tteam is the team’s best time including penalties.
  • Tmin is the fastest vehicle time including penalties.
  • Tmax is 145% of the fastest vehicle time including penalties.

docs.title: D6.5.1
docs.text: 10 points are awarded to every team that finishes at least one run without DNF or DQ.

docs.title: D6.5.2
docs.text:
If a team’s corrected elapsed time is below Tmax, points based on the following formula are given:

[ \textit{AUTOCROSS_SCORE}{i} = 90\left(\frac{T\right) ]} - T_{team,i}}{T_{max} - T_{min}

[ \textit{AUTOCROSS_SCORE}{total} = max(\textit{AUTOCROSS_SCORE}}, avg(\textit{AUTOCROSS_SCORE{1}..\textit{AUTOCROSS_SCORE})) ]

  • Tteam,i is the team’s time including penalties of run i.
  • Tmax is the time for driving the lap with 4m/s.
  • Tmin is the fastest corrected elapsed time of all teams.

docs.title: D7.1.1
docs.text: The endurance track layout is a closed lap circuit built to the following guidelines: - Straights: No longer than 80m - Constant Turns: up to 50m diameter - Hairpin Turns: Minimum of 9m outside diameter (of the turn) - Slaloms: Cones in a straight line with 9m to 15m spacing - Miscellaneous: Chicanes, multiple turns, decreasing radius turns, etc. - The minimum track width is 3m

docs.title: D7.1.2
docs.text: The length of one lap of the endurance track is approximately 1km.

docs.title: D7.1.3
docs.text: The length of the complete endurance is approximately 22km.

docs.title: D7.1.4
docs.text: The organisers reserve the right to deviate from the parameters specified, when they determine it is appropriate given the characteristics of the particular competition site.

docs.title: D7.2.1
docs.text: Before entering the event, each CV’s fuel tank must be filled to the fuel level line (see CV2.6.4, “Fuel Level Line”) at the fuelling station. During fuelling, once filled to the scribe line, no shaking or tilting of the tank, the fuel system or the entire vehicle is allowed.

docs.title: D7.2.2
docs.text: There is only one run for the endurance event.

docs.title: D7.2.3
docs.text: A driver change must be made at the midpoint of the run.

docs.title: D7.2.4
docs.text: Staging - The vehicle is staged at a staging line prior to the starting line. If the vehicle is unable to proceed across the timing line from the staging line due to a vehicle issue, then a DNS (Did Not Start) will be applied, it has failed the endurance event and will not be allowed to be repaired and re-start

docs.title: D7.2.5
docs.text: Starting - A green flag is used to indicate that the driver may start. Timing starts only after the vehicle crosses the starting line.

docs.title: D7.2.6
docs.text: The first driver will drive for 11km and will then be signalled into the driver change area.

docs.title: D7.2.7
docs.text: After the driver change specified in D7.5, the second driver will drive for an additional 11km and will be signalled to exit the track after crossing the finish line.

docs.title: D7.2.8
docs.text: After leaving the track, the vehicle must be powered down.

docs.title: D7.2.9
docs.text: For CV, the second driver will proceed directly to the fuelling station. The tank will be filled to the refill mark and the amount of fuel will be recorded.

docs.title: D7.3.1
docs.text: The running order for the endurance will be established in a way that vehicles with similar speeds shall be on the track together.

docs.title: D7.3.2
docs.text: The running order will be published at Event Control.

docs.title: D7.4.1
docs.text: During the endurance event, overtaking is only permissible in the designated passing zones and under the control of the track marshals.

docs.title: D7.4.2
docs.text: Passing zones have two parallel lanes, a slow lane only used by the vehicles that are being overtaken and a fast lane for the vehicles that are overtaking.

docs.title: D7.4.3
docs.text: Passing zones may be situated on either the left or right of the fast lane.

docs.title: D7.4.4
docs.text: The passing zone procedure will be as follows: - A slower leading vehicle will be shown the blue flag and must drive into the slow lane and decelerate, - The following faster vehicle will continue in the fast lane to pass the slow vehicle, - The vehicle that has been overtaken may re-enter the track when the track marshal who is in charge of that passing zone is showing the green flag.

docs.title: D7.4.5
docs.text: The passing rules do not apply to vehicles that are stopped on track or vehicles that have spun out and are not moving. When passing a stationary vehicle, it is critical to slow down, drive cautiously and to follow the instructions from the track marshals.

docs.title: D7.5.1
docs.text: Only three team members including the driver may enter the driver change area. They may only bring the tools required to adjust the vehicle to accommodate the second driver and/or change tyres.

docs.title: D7.5.2
docs.text: For electric vehicles one of the team members must be an ESO.

docs.title: D7.5.3
docs.text:
During the driver change, the team may: - perform changes to accommodate the second driver, - operate the master switch(es), - change tyres as per D7.6.

No other work may be performed during the driver change, external jumper batteries may not be used to restart the car

docs.title: D7.5.4
docs.text: Each team is given three minutes to change their driver and one minute to restart the car.

docs.title: D7.5.5
docs.text: The driver change time will start once the vehicle is stopped in the driver change area and the first driver has turned off the engine for CV or turned off the tractive system for EVs.

docs.title: D7.5.6
docs.text: [EV ONLY] The TSMS must be switched off by the ESO and the TSAL must have changed to green colour, before anyone is allowed to touch the vehicle or to climb out the vehicle.

docs.title: D7.5.7
docs.text: The first driver will climb out the vehicle and any necessary adjustments will be made to the vehicle to fit the second driver (seat cushions, head restraint, pedal position, etc.). The second driver will then be secured in the vehicle.

docs.title: D7.5.8
docs.text: When the second driver is fully secured in the vehicle, the driver change time ends. Marshalls will check that the driver is securely fastened into the vehicle and complies with all regulations.

docs.title: D7.5.9
docs.text: The driver will be given the signal to start the engine/tractive system. The moment the signal is given, the driver is given one minute to restart the car.

docs.title: D7.5.10
docs.text: Once the vehicle has restarted and is ready-to-drive again, the restart time is stopped.

docs.title: D7.5.11
docs.text: If the driver change and vehicle starting takes longer than three minutes and one minute, respectively, the extra time is included in the final time.

docs.title: D7.6.1
docs.text: All tyre changes after a vehicle has received the green flag to start the endurance event must take place in the driver change area.

docs.title: D7.6.2
docs.text: If the operating condition changes to wet during endurance, the track will be red flagged, and all vehicles brought into the driver change area.

docs.title: D7.6.3
docs.text: If a team wants to change tyres, the officials must be informed beforehand.

docs.title: D7.6.4
docs.text: In some cases, tyre changes can be carried out directly after the driver change, for others the team must make an extra stop.

docs.title: D7.6.5
docs.text: The allowed tyre changes and associated conditions are given in the following tables.

docs.title: Table 14: Allowed tyre changes
docs.text:
Existing Operating Condition Currently running on Condition changes to Dry Condition changes to Damp Condition changes to Wet Dry Dry Tyres – A B Damp Dry Tyres – A B Damp Wet Tyres C C – Wet Wet Tyres C C – Requirement Allowed at Driver Change? Time Allowed A may change from dry to wet yes Note 1 B must change from dry to wet yes Note 1 C may change from wet to dry no Note 2

Allowed tyre changes

Note 1: Any time in excess of ten minutes without driver change, or thirteen minutes with driver change, is added to the team’s total time for endurance.

Note 2: The time used to change to dry tyres is added to the team’s total time for endurance.

docs.title: D7.6.6
docs.text: Teams that have incurred a puncture during the endurance event due to external factors (e.g. debris on track) may change the tyre with no time penalty, if the vehicle reaches the driver change area under its own power without external assistance.

docs.title: D7.6.7
docs.text: The wheel will be inspected by the officials. If the deflation was not caused by external factors, the vehicle will be scored DNF.

docs.title: D7.6.8
docs.text: Deflation caused by running off-course or impacting barriers or other objects due to driver error will not be regarded as external factors.

docs.title: D7.6.9
docs.text: If a vehicle is unable to maintain lap times within one hundred forty-five percent (145%) of the fastest lap time for the course, then it must exit immediately.

docs.title: D7.6.10
docs.text: Disqualification for failure to maintain the minimum speed will be made at the discretion of the Dynamic Event Captain / Clerk of the Course.

docs.title: D7.7.1
docs.text: Teams are prohibited from working on or fuelling their vehicles during the run.

docs.title: D7.7.2
docs.text: Wheel-to-wheel racing is prohibited.

docs.title: D7.7.3
docs.text: Passing another vehicle must be completed as per D7.4.

docs.title: D7.7.4
docs.text: If a vehicle stops on track, it is allowed one minute to restart.

docs.title: D7.7.5
docs.text: If a vehicle has a restart problem at the driver change or after a red flag, it is allowed two minutes to restart the engine, enable the tractive system or to enter R2D. The two minutes start from the time the driver first tries to restart. The time is counted towards the endurance time.

docs.title: D7.7.6
docs.text: If restarts are not accomplished within the above times, the vehicle is scored as DNF for the run.

docs.title: D7.7.7
docs.text: If a vehicle breaks down, it will be removed from the track and will not be allowed to re- enter the track.

docs.title: D7.7.8
docs.text: Team members may be instructed by the officials to retrieve broken down vehicles. This recovery may only be carried out under the control of the officials.

docs.title: D7.8.1
docs.text: Each lap of the endurance event is individually timed. The corrected elapsed time is determined by subtracting the extra-long lap for the driver change from the total time and adding any penalty times.

docs.title: D7.8.2
docs.text: The post event technical inspection (see IN12) must be passed to score points in the endurance event.

docs.title: D7.8.3
docs.text: 25 points are awarded to every team that finishes endurance without DNF or DQ.

docs.title: D7.8.4
docs.text:
If a team’s corrected elapsed time is below Tmax, additional points based on the following formula are given:

[ \textit{ENDURANCE SCORE} = 225\left(\frac{\frac{T_{max}}{T_{team}} - 1}{\frac{T_{max}}{T_{min}} - 1}\right) ]

  • Tteam is the team’s best time including penalties.
  • Tmin is the fastest vehicle time including penalties.
  • Tmax is 145% of the fastest vehicle time including penalties.

docs.title: D7.8.5
docs.text:
If a team DNFs then:

[ \textit{ENDURANCE SCORE} = \text{Number of Laps Completed} ]

docs.title: D7.8.6
docs.text: It a driver’s run is interrupted by a red flag, the recorded lap time for their red-flagged lap will be replaced by the average lap time from their preceding laps. The number of laps used for the averaging will be at the discretion of the Dynamic Event Captain.

docs.title: D7.9.1
docs.text: The Efficiency is based on a metric of the amount of fuel consumed or energy used and the lap time on the endurance course, averaged over the length of the event. Teams are advised that the Efficiency score is based only on the distance cars run on the course during the Endurance event. Although the starting line, exit line and the driver change zone increase the actual distance a car must drive during the event, those distances are not factored into the fuel calculations. Additionally, fuel consumption adjustments will not be made for engine running in the entry/exit lines, during driver change, in the penalty box or for any on-course incidents. The Organisers may use either the corrected Endurance lap times or the scored Endurance lap times for the Efficiency event.

docs.title: D7.9.2
docs.text: The mass of CO2 released to the atmosphere will be assessed by using the conversion factors below from quantity of fuel used to CO2 released. The factors are intended to represent the average supply of the appropriate commodity and the Organisers will not take account of where the actual fuel used came from.

docs.title: Table 15: Fuel Conversion Factors
docs.text:
Fuel Type Conversion Factor E10 gasoline 799g CO₂ per litre Electric 143g CO₂ per kWh E85 571g CO₂ per litre

Fuel Conversion Factors

The conversion factor for Alternative Fuels will be determined by the organisers upon receipt and review of the Alternative Fuel Report.

docs.title: D7.9.3
docs.text: Full credit will be given for energy recovered through regenerative braking.

docs.title: D7.9.4
docs.text:
Efficiency will be scored using the following formulas:

[ \textit{EFFICIENCY SCORE} = 100\left(\frac{\left(\frac{EfficiencyFactor_{min}}{EfficiencyFactor_{team}}\right) - 1}{\left(\frac{EfficiencyFactor_{min}}{EfficiencyFactor_{max}}\right) - 1}\right) ]

[ \textit{EFFICIENCY FACTOR} = \frac{T_{min}/LapTotal_{Tmin}}{T_{team}/Laps_{team}} * \frac{CO_{2min}/LapTotal_{CO2min}}{CO_{2team}/Laps_{team}} ]

Where:

 CO2min is the smallest mass of CO2 used by any competitor whose endurance time Tteam is less than 145% of the average lap time of the fastest team that completes the endurance event.  CO2team is the mass of CO2 used by the team being scored.  Tmin is the lowest Endurance time of the fastest team whose fuel consumption does not exceed 26 litres/100km or energy equivalent of 20 kgCO2/100km.  Tteam is the combined Endurance times of the drivers in your heat.  Lapsteam is the number of laps driven by the team being scored.  LapTotalTmin and LapTotalCO2min are the number of laps completed by the teams which set Tmin and CO2min respectively.  EfficiencyFactormin is calculated using CO2team equivalent to 20 kgCO2/100km and Tteam set to 145% of the average laptime of the fastest team that completes the Endurance event.

docs.title: D7.9.5
docs.text: Vehicles whose average Endurance lap time exceeds 1.45 times the average Endurance lap time of the fastest team that completes the Endurance event, will receive zero (0) points for efficiency.

docs.title: D7.9.6
docs.text: Vehicles whose corrected average fuel consumption per lap exceeds 26 litres/100 km or energy equivalent of 20 kgCO2/100 km, will receive zero (0) points for Efficiency.

docs.title: D7.9.7
docs.text: The minimum Efficiency Factor is determined from the maximum allowable CO2/100km and 145% of the corrected average Endurance lap time of the fastest team that completes the Endurance event.

docs.title: D7.9.8
docs.text: Efficiency scores can range from zero points (0) to positive one hundred (100) points.

docs.title: D7.9.9
docs.text: Vehicles which cross the start line following driver change are eligible for Efficiency points. Other vehicles will receive a score of zero points (0) for Efficiency.

docs.title: D7.9.10
docs.text: Should the fuel level change after refuelling due to effects such as described in CV2.7.1 then the difference in fuel level will be measured and twice the amount will be added to the official fuel consumption figure.

docs.title: D8.1.1
docs.text: The trackdrive layout is a closed loop circuit built to the following guidelines: - Straights: No longer than 80m, - Constant Turns: up to 50m diameter, - Hairpin Turns: Minimum of 9m outside diameter (of the turn), - Miscellaneous: Chicanes, multiple turns, decreasing radius turns, etc, - The minimum track width is 3m.

docs.title: D8.1.2
docs.text: The length of one lap is approximately 200m to 500m.

docs.title: D8.2.1
docs.text: Starting order may be defined by the officials, based on previous dynamic event results.

docs.title: D8.2.2
docs.text: Before starting a run, each vehicle with a fuel tank (CV), must be filled to the fuel level line (see CV2.6.4, “Fuel Level Line”) at the fuelling station. During fuelling, once filled to the scribe line, no shaking or tilting of the tank, the fuel system or the entire vehicle is allowed.

docs.title: D8.2.3
docs.text: There will be a maximum of two runs, each run consisting of ten laps. The number of runs and the starting order procedure will be announced before the start of the event.

docs.title: D8.2.4
docs.text: Staging - The vehicle is staged such that the front wheels are 6 m in front of the starting line on the track.

docs.title: D8.2.5
docs.text: Starting - A go-signal from RES is used to indicate the approval to begin. Timing starts after the vehicle crosses the starting line.

docs.title: D8.2.6
docs.text: After ten laps the vehicle must come to a full stop within 30m behind the finish line on the track and enter the finish-state described in T14.9.

docs.title: D8.2.7
docs.text: There will be no last lap signal i.e. the vehicle should count laps itself.

docs.title: D8.2.8
docs.text: The team must proceed directly to the fuelling station (vehicles with internal combustion engine only).

docs.title: D8.3.1
docs.text: If there is more than one run per vehicle, the run with the highest score of trackdrive is scored.

docs.title: D8.3.2
docs.text: Tmax and Tmin for the trackdrive score is calculated based on all valid runs.

docs.title: D8.3.3
docs.text: Each lap of the trackdrive event is individually timed. The corrected elapsed time is determined by adding any penalty times.

docs.title: D8.3.4
docs.text:
If a team’s corrected elapsed time is below Tmax and the run was not DNF or DQ, points based on the following formula are given:

[ \textit{TRACKDRIVE_SCORE} = 150\left(\frac{T_{max}}{T_{min}}\right) ]

  • Tteam is the team’s corrected elapsed time.
  • Tmax is 2 times of the corrected elapsed time of the fastest vehicle over all runs.

docs.title: D8.3.5
docs.text: An additional five points are awarded for every completed lap, independent of the corrected elapsed time. This is also applied for teams that do not finish the trackdrive i.e. get a DNF.

docs.title: D9.1.1
docs.text: Penalties will not be assessed for accident avoidance or other reasons deemed sufficient by the officials.

docs.title: D9.1.2
docs.text: A cone is Down or Out (DOO) if the cone has been knocked over or the entire base of the cone lies outside the box marked around the cone in its undisturbed position.

docs.title: D9.1.3
docs.text: Cones that are DOO are not replaced/reset during a DV run. There will be no re-run due to cones in the driving path or disorientation due to missing cones.

docs.title: D9.1.4
docs.text: The DOO penalty (see D9.1.7) is added for each DOO including entry and exit gate cones before the start and after the finish line, which occur on that particular run.

docs.title: D9.1.5
docs.text: Off-course (OC) - An OC occurs when the vehicle has all four wheels outside the track boundary as indicated by edge marking, - Missing one or more gates of a given slalom at autocross or endurance is counted as one OC per occurrence, - When an OC occurs, the driver must re-enter the track at the next possible point, - When re-entering the driver needs to wait for a gap and follow the instructions of the track marshals.

docs.title: D9.1.6
docs.text: An Unsafe Stop (USS) is defined as not stopping within the specified area and/or not entering the finish-state described in T14.9 within 30 seconds during autonomous running.

docs.title: Table 16: Dynamic event penalties
docs.text:
Acceleration Skidpad Autocross Endurance Trackdrive DOO 2s 0.2s 2s 2s 2s OC DNF DNF 10s 10s 10s USS DNF DNF DNF N/A −50 points

Dynamic event penalties

docs.title: D9.1.8
docs.text: DNF equals zero points for that run.

docs.title: D9.1.9
docs.text: DQ equals zero points for that run.

docs.title: D9.1.10
docs.text: If a team Did Not Attempt (DNA) an event the score is zero points.

docs.title: D9.1.11
docs.text: Each run with an incorrect number of laps at skidpad is classified as DNF.

docs.title: D9.1.12
docs.text: Failure to obey a marshal or a flag: one minute time penalty.

docs.title: D9.1.13
docs.text: Reckless or aggressive driving or “Over Driving”: Black Flag (see D2.1.9), additional time penalties (up to a maximum of five minutes) may also be applied. If the driver continues to drive recklessly or aggressively after being black flagged, they may be DQ’d.

docs.title: D9.1.14
docs.text: Vehicle to vehicle contact: Two minutes up to disqualification depending on the nature of the incident.

docs.title: D9.1.15
docs.text: If a vehicle stops and cannot restart without external assistance, the vehicle is DNF for that run.

docs.title: D9.1.16
docs.text: If a vehicle is not able to start the run, after being called to the staging/starting line, the vehicle is DQ for that run.

docs.title: D9.2.1
docs.text: Teams that are running out-of-order as defined in the competition handbook, are penalized by two minutes and may then run at the discretion of the officials.

docs.title: D9.2.2
docs.text: Mechanical Problem: The time taken for mechanical inspection under a “mechanical black flag” (see D2.1.10) is considered officials’ time and is not included in the team’s total time. If the inspection reveals a mechanical integrity problem the vehicle is scored DNF.

docs.title: D9.2.3
docs.text: If it is impossible to impose a penalty by a stop under a black flag, e.g. not enough laps left, the officials may add an appropriate time penalty to the team’s elapsed time.

docs.title: D9.2.4
docs.text: A team may receive a DNF if their vehicle is too slow or being driven without proper control.

docs.title: D9.2.5
docs.text: Any violation to the procedure of driver change (D7.5.3) will lead to a time penalty of up to two minutes.

docs.title: D9.3.1
docs.text: Should the fuel level change after refuelling due to effects such as described in CV2.7.1, then the difference in fuel level will be measured and twice the amount will be added to the official fuel consumption figure.

docs.title: D9.4 [EV ONLY] Power and Voltage Violation Penalties
D9.4.1
docs.text: A violation is defined as using more than the maximum power, see EV2.2, or exceeding the specified voltage, see EV4.1.1, after a moving average over 500ms is applied to the respective Energy Meter signal, see EV4.6.

docs.title: D9.4.2
docs.text: Each violation is a DQ for the fastest run of the event. If a violation occurred during two runs, the two fastest runs will be DQ etc.

docs.title: D9.4.3
docs.text: The respective data and the resulting decision of violations may be made public.

docs.title: D9.4.4
docs.text: Non-availability of Energy Meter data will be treated as a violation.

docs.title: EV1.1.1
docs.text: Tractive System (TS) – every part that is electrically connected to the motor(s) and TS accumulators. The LVS may be supplied by the TS if a galvanic isolation between both systems is ensured.

docs.title: EV1.1.2
docs.text: TS Enclosures – every housing or enclosure containing parts of the TS.

docs.title: EV1.2.1
docs.text:
Galvanic Isolation – two electric circuits are defined as galvanically isolated, if all of the following conditions are true: - The resistance between both circuits is ≥500 Ω/V, related to the maximum TS voltage of the vehicle, at a test voltage of maximum TS voltage or 250 V, whichever is higher. - The isolation test voltage RMS, AC for 1 min, between both circuits is higher than three times the maximum TS voltage or 750 V, whichever is higher. - The working voltage of the isolation barrier is higher than the maximum TS voltage.

Capacitors that bridge galvanic isolation must be class-Y capacitors

docs.title: EV1.2.2
docs.text: High Current Path – any path of a TS circuitry that, during normal operation, carries more than 1A.

docs.title: EV2.1.1
docs.text: Only electric motors are allowed.

docs.title: EV2.1.2
docs.text: Motor attachments must follow T10.

docs.title: EV2.1.3
docs.text: Motor casings must follow T7.3.

docs.title: EV2.1.4
docs.text: The motor(s) must be connected to the accumulator through a motor controller.

docs.title: EV2.2.1
docs.text: The TS power, measured by the Energy Meter, must not exceed +80kW or 500A, whichever is lower.

docs.title: EV2.2.2
docs.text: Negative TS power (regenerating energy), measured by the Energy Meter, is permissible and unrestricted for power, but the 500A current limit applies.

docs.title: EV2.2.3
docs.text: Supplying power to the motor(s) such that the car is driven in reverse is prohibited.

docs.title: EV2.3 APPS / Brake Pedal Plausibility Check
EV2.3.1
docs.text:
The commanded motor torque must be 0 Nm, if the mechanical brakes are actuated and the APPS, see T11.8, signals pedal travel equivalent to >25% desired motor torque or

5kW, whichever is lower, at the same time, for longer than 500ms.

docs.title: EV2.3.2
docs.text: The commanded motor torque must remain at 0Nm until the APPS signals less than 5% pedal travel and 0Nm desired motor torque, regardless of whether the brakes are still actuated or not.

docs.title: EV3.1.1
docs.text: TS Enclosures, see EV1.1.2, must consist of either: - A grounded solid layer made of at least 0.5 mm thick electrically conductive material, aluminium or better, see EV3.1.3, or - Be made from electrically insulating materials providing an isolation resistance of at least 2 MΩ, measured with a voltage of 500 V, between the inside and the outside of the enclosure. The enclosure must be rigid and must prevent possible mechanical penetrations. Protruding electrically conductive parts, such as fasteners or connectors, must follow EV3.1.2.

docs.title: EV3.1.2
docs.text: Electrically conductive seat, driver harness, and firewall mounting points as well as the aluminium layer of the TS firewall, see T4.8, and the LVS ground measuring point, see EV4.7.8, must be grounded, see EV3.1.3.

docs.title: EV3.1.3
docs.text: An electrically conductive part is grounded if its resistance to LVS ground is below 100mΩ, measured with a current of 1 A, and the grounding wire is able to continuously carry at least 10 % of the TS accumulator main fuse current rating.

docs.title: EV3.1.4
docs.text: Parts of the vehicle which may become electrically conductive (e.g. completely coated metal parts, carbon fibre parts, etc.) within 100mm of any TS component must have a resistance below 100Ω to LVS ground.

docs.title: EV3.1.5
docs.text: The rotating part of the wheels does not need to be grounded.

docs.title: EV3.2.1
docs.text: All electrical systems must have appropriate overcurrent protection.

docs.title: EV3.2.2
docs.text: The continuous current rating of the overcurrent protection must not be greater than the continuous current rating of any electrical component, for example wire, busbar or other conductor that it protects. i.e. if multiple pins of a connector are used to carry currents in parallel, each pin must be appropriately protected.

docs.title: EV3.2.3
docs.text: All fuses must have an interrupt current rating which is higher than the theoretical short circuit current of the system that it protects.

docs.title: EV3.2.4
docs.text: All overcurrent protection devices must be rated for the highest voltage in the systems they protect. All devices used must be rated for DC.

docs.title: EV3.2.5
docs.text: All overcurrent protection devices that are part of the TS must not rely on programmable logic. The overcurrent protection function of unmodified commercially available motor controllers/inverters for the motor outputs may rely on programmable logic.

docs.title: EV3.2.6
docs.text: The overcurrent protection must be designed for the expected surrounding temperature range but at least for 0°C to 85 °C

docs.title: EV3.2.7
docs.text: The TS high current path through the accumulator(s) must be fused.

docs.title: EV4.1.1
docs.text: The maximum permitted voltage that may occur between any two electrical connections is 600VDC and for motor controller/inverters and Accumulator Management System (AMS) internal low power control signals 630 VDC.

docs.title: EV4.1.2
docs.text: All components in the TS must be rated for the maximum TS voltage. The TS area of a PCB, see EV4.3.6, is considered as one component. Every input connected to the TS must be rated to the maximum TS voltage.

docs.title: EV4.1.3
docs.text: All components must be rated for the maximum possible temperature that may occur during use.

docs.title: EV4.1.4
docs.text: Fans with >50W power must not be connected to the TS.

docs.title: EV4.2.1
docs.text: Every housing or enclosure containing parts of the TS system, must be labelled with (a) reasonably sized sticker(s) according to “ISO 7010-W012” (triangle with black lightning bolt on yellow background). The sticker must also contain the text “High Voltage” if the voltage is more than 60VDC or 25VAC.

docs.title: EV4.3 Separation of Traction System and Grounded Low Voltage System
EV4.3.1
docs.text: The entire TS and LVS must be galvanically isolated, see EV1.2.1 and IN4.1.1.

docs.title: EV4.3.2
docs.text: All connections from a TS component to external devices, such as laptops must include galvanic isolation, see EV1.2.1.

docs.title: EV4.3.3
docs.text: TS and LVS circuits must be physically segregated such that they are not running through the same conduit or connector, except for interlock circuit connections.

docs.title: EV4.3.4
docs.text: Where both TS and LVS are present within an TS enclosure, they must be separated by barriers made of moisture-resistant insulating materials or maintain 20 mm spacing through air, or over a surface.

docs.title: EV4.3.5
docs.text: Components and cables capable of movement must be positively restrained to maintain spacing.

docs.title: EV4.3.6
docs.text:
If TS and LVS are on the same PCB, they must be on separate well defined areas of the board, meeting the spacing requirements in Table 4, each area clearly marked with “TS” or “LV”. The outline of the area required for spacing must be marked.

Grooves and cut-outs must have a minimum width of 1.5 mm to influence the creepage path. “Conformal coating” refers to a coating insulator on a PCB. Solder resist is not a coating.

docs.title: Table 4: Spacing required between TS and LV
docs.text:
Voltage Clearance Distance Creepage DistanceGeneral Creepage DistanceConformal Coating 0VDC to 50VDC 1.0mm 4mm 1.0mm 50VDC to 150VDC 1.0mm 5mm 1.0mm 150VDC to 300VDC 1.5mm 10mm 2.0mm 300VDC to 600VDC 3.0mm 20mm 4.0mm

Spacing required between TS and LV

docs.title: EV4.3.7
docs.text: Teams must be prepared to demonstrate spacing on team-built equipment. For inaccessible circuitry, spare boards must be available. These do not have to be fully assembled.

docs.title: EV4.4 Positioning of Tractive System Parts
EV4.4.1
docs.text: With the exception of what is permitted according to EV4.4.4, all parts belonging to the TS including cables and wiring must be located within the rollover protection envelope, see T1.1.16. “Part” is the whole device such as the complete HVD.

docs.title: EV4.4.2
docs.text: Any part of the TS that is less than 350 mm above the ground, except items permitted by EV4.4.3, must be protected from impacts according to T3.15 and must follow T3.16 when having bolted attachments.

docs.title: EV4.4.3
docs.text: TS wiring in front of the front roll hoop may alternatively be shielded by the front bulkhead support structure according to T3.14.

docs.title: EV4.4.4
docs.text: Outboard wheel motors are allowed only if: - Interlocks are routed such that the shutdown circuit, see EV6.1, is opened before the TS wiring or its connection fails, or in the event of a suspension failure - TS wiring is not able to reach the cockpit opening or the driver regardless of where it breaks - Wiring outside of the rollover protection envelope, see T1.1.16, is minimum length. - Wiring outside of an impact structure or front bulkhead support structure, see EV4.4.2, is minimum length. - Minimum length is the shortest distance plus extra wiring required for suspension / steering travel and bend radii.

docs.title: EV4.4.5
docs.text: In side or front view any part of the TS must not project below the lower surface of the chassis.

docs.title: EV4.4.6
docs.text: Additional regulations apply for TS accumulators, see EV5.5.

docs.title: EV4.5 Tractive System Insulation, Wiring and Conduit
EV4.5.1
docs.text: All live parts of the TS must be protected from being touched. This must include team members working on or inside the vehicle. This is tested with a 100mm long, 6mm diameter insulated test probe when the TS enclosures are in place.

docs.title: EV4.5.2
docs.text: Insulation material that is rated for the maximum TS voltage must be used. Using only insulating tape or rubber-like paint for insulation is prohibited.

docs.title: EV4.5.3
docs.text: The temperature rating for TS wiring, connections and insulation must be appropriate for the expected surrounding temperatures but at least 85 °C.

docs.title: EV4.5.4
docs.text: TS components and containers must be protected from moisture in the form of rain or puddles to a minimum of IPX2, see IN9.

docs.title: EV4.5.5
docs.text: It must be possible to clearly assign and prove wire gauge, temperature rating and insulation voltage to each used wire.

docs.title: EV4.5.6
docs.text: All TS wiring must be completed to professional standards with appropriately sized conductors and terminals and with adequate strain relief and protection from loosening due to vibration etc.

docs.title: EV4.5.7
docs.text: TS wiring must be located out of the way of possible snagging or damage.

docs.title: EV4.5.8
docs.text:
All TS wiring that runs outside of TS enclosures must - Be enclosed in separate orange non-conductive conduit or use an orange shielded cable. The conduit must be securely anchored to the vehicle, but not to wire, at least at each end, - Be securely anchored at least at each end so that it can withstand a force of 200N without straining the cable end crimp.

Bodywork is not sufficient to meet this enclosure requirement.

docs.title: EV4.5.9
docs.text: Any shielded cable must have the shield grounded.

docs.title: EV4.5.10
docs.text: Every TS connector outside of a housing must include a pilot contact/interlock line which is part of the shutdown circuit. Housings only used to avoid interlocks are prohibited.

docs.title: EV4.5.11
docs.text: All TS connections must be designed so that they use intentional current paths through conductors such as copper or aluminium and should not rely on steel bolts to be the primary conductor.

docs.title: EV4.5.12
docs.text:
All TS connections must not include compressible material such as plastic in the stack-up or as a fastener. FR-4 is allowed.

NOTE: This rule has been reworked in the Formula Student Germany 2026 Rules, if you plan to compete at other events, you must ensure you are compliant with that rule.

docs.title: EV4.5.13
docs.text: TS connectors outside of TS enclosures must be designed in a way, that the TS cannot be activated, see EV4.11, if connected in any way other than the design intent configuration.

docs.title: EV4.5.14
docs.text:
All electrical connections, including bolts, nuts and other fasteners, in the high current path of the TS must be secured from unintentional loosening by the use of positive locking mechanisms that are suitable for high temperatures, see T10.2.

Components, e.g. inverters, certified for automotive use might be allowed without positive locking feature, if connections are completed as recommended by the manufacturers datasheet and no positive locking is possible.

The team must be able to demonstrate that they have assessed the risk of loosening of these connections and describe this and the control methods applied in their ESF.

docs.title: EV4.5.15
docs.text: Teams must be prepared to demonstrate positive locking. For inaccessible connections, appropriate photographs must be available.

docs.title: EV4.5.16
docs.text: Soldered connections in the high current path are only allowed if all of the following are true: - Connections on PCBs, - The connected devices are not cells or wires, - The devices are additionally mechanically secured against loosening.

docs.title: EV4.6.1
docs.text: A calibrated Energy Meter will be provided by the officials and must be inserted during competition. The Energy Meter measures TS voltage and TS current.

docs.title: EV4.6.2
docs.text: The Datalogger module of the Energy Meter must be in an easily accessible location so that it is possible for the officials to check its operation and insert/remove the memory stick at any time.

docs.title: EV4.6.3
docs.text: The Energy Meter must not be installed within the TSAC.

docs.title: EV4.6.4
docs.text: All current supplying the TS must run through the Energy Meter. The Energy Meter must be inserted in the negative TS supply between the most negative AIR(s) and the inverters.

docs.title: EV4.6.5
docs.text: The TS voltage sense connection of the Energy Meter must be directly connected, see T1.3.1, to the most positive AIR(s) on vehicle side.

docs.title: EV4.6.6
docs.text: The Energy Meter LV connection must be supplied from the LVMS. The Energy Meter requires a stable 12V supply, so regulators or voltage converters are permitted if necessary. There should be no switching or relays between the LV source and the Energy Meter.

docs.title: EV4.6.7
docs.text: The specification of the Energy Meter will be available on the Formula Student website.

docs.title: EV4.7.1
docs.text: Two TSMPs must be installed directly next to the master switches, see EV6.2.

docs.title: EV4.7.2
docs.text: The TSMPs must be directly connected, see T1.3.1, to the intermediate circuit capacitors even if the HVD has been opened or the TS accumulator is disconnected.

docs.title: EV4.7.3
docs.text: 4mm shrouded banana jacks of rated for 1000 V CAT III or better must be used.

docs.title: EV4.7.4
docs.text: The TSMPs must be marked “TS+” and “TS-” and exclusively mounted on orange back- ground.

docs.title: EV4.7.5
docs.text: The TSMPs must be protected by a non-conductive housing that can be opened without tools. The cover must always be mechanically linked to the vehicle.

docs.title: EV4.7.6
docs.text: Each TSMP must be secured with a current limiting resistor according to Table 5, below. Fusing of the TSMPs is prohibited. The resistors power rating must be chosen such that they are able to continuously carry the current if both TSMPs are short circuited.

docs.title: Table 5: TSMP Resistor requirements
docs.text:
Maximum TS Voltage Resistor Value Umax <200 VDC 5kΩ 200 VDC <Umax ≤400 VDC 10kΩ 400 VDC <Umax ≤600 VDC 15kΩ

TSMP Resistor requirements

docs.title: EV4.7.7
docs.text: All electrical connections needed for TSMP, including bolts, nuts and other fasteners, must be secured from unintentional loosening by the use of positive locking mechanisms. Bolted connections must follow T10.2, soldered connections EV4.5.16

docs.title: EV4.7.8
docs.text: Next to the TSMPs, a LVS ground measuring point must be installed. A 4mm black shrouded banana jack must be connected to LVS ground and must be marked “GND”.

docs.title: EV4.8.1
docs.text: It must be possible to disconnect at least one pole of the TS accumulator by quickly removing an unobstructed and directly accessible element, fuse or connector. It must be possible to disconnect the HVD without removing any bodywork. The HVD must be above 350mm from the ground and easily visible when standing behind the vehicle. Remote actuation of the HVD through a long handle, rope or wire is not permitted.

docs.title: EV4.8.2
docs.text: An untrained person must be able to remove the HVD within 10s when the vehicle is in ready-to-race condition.

docs.title: EV4.8.3
docs.text: A dummy connector or similar may be required to restore the system’s isolation, see EV4.5. The dummy connector must be green and clearly identifiable to an observer when in use. It must be attached to the push bar, see T1.3.1, if not in use.

docs.title: EV4.8.4
docs.text: The HVD must be clearly marked with “HVD”.

docs.title: EV4.8.5
docs.text: No tools must be necessary to open the HVD. An interlock is required, see EV4.5.10.

docs.title: EV4.9.1
docs.text:
If a discharge circuit is required to meet EV6.1.5, it must be designed to handle the maximum TS voltage permanently.

After three subsequent discharges within 15s in total, the discharge time specified in EV6.1.5 may be exceeded. Full discharging functionality must be given after a reasonable time with a deactivated discharge circuit.

docs.title: EV4.9.2
docs.text: The discharge circuit must be wired in a way that it is always active whenever the shutdown circuit is open. Furthermore, the discharge circuit must be fail-safe such that it still discharges the intermediate circuit capacitors if the HVD has been opened or the TS accumulator is disconnected.

docs.title: EV4.9.3
docs.text: Fusing of the main current discharge path is prohibited.

docs.title: EV4.10.1
docs.text: The vehicle must include a single TSAL that must indicate the TS status. The TSAL must not perform any other functions. A TSAL with multiple LEDs in one housing is allowed.

docs.title: EV4.10.2
docs.text: The TSAL itself must have a red light, flashing continuously with a frequency between 2Hz and 5Hz and a duty cycle of 50%, active whenever the LVS is active and for at least 15 minutes after it is switched off (see Ev4.10.16) and the voltage across any DC-link capacitor exceeds the lower of either: - 60VDC or 50VACRMS, - Half the nominal TS voltage.

docs.title: EV4.10.3
docs.text: The TSAL itself must have a green light, continuously on, active whenever the LVS is active and for at least 15 minutes after it is switched off (see EV4.10.16) and ALL of the following conditions are true: - All AIRs are opened. - The pre-charge relay, see EV5.7.2, is opened. - The voltage at the vehicle side of the AIRs inside the TSAC does not exceed 60VDC or 50VACRMS.

docs.title: EV4.10.4
docs.text: The voltage detection for the TSAL must be performed inside the respective TS enclosure.

docs.title: EV4.10.5
docs.text: The described states of the relays (opened/closed) are the actual mechanical states. The mechanical state can differ from the intentional state, i.e. if a relay is stuck. Any circuitry detecting the mechanical state must meet EV5.6.2.

docs.title: EV4.10.6
docs.text: The voltage detection circuit of the red light and the relay state and voltage detection circuit of the green light must be independent. Any plausibility check between both lights is not allowed. A TSAL state with both lights simultaneously active might occur and must not be prevented.

docs.title: EV4.10.7
docs.text: The TSAL must: - Be located lower than the highest point of the main hoop and including the mounting within the rollover protection envelope, see T1.1.16. - Be no lower than 75mm from the highest point of the main hoop. - Not be able to contact the driver’s helmet in any circumstances.

docs.title: EV4.10.8
docs.text: The entire illuminated surface of the TSAL must be clearly visible: - Except for angles less than 10° on each side which are blocked by the main hoop. - From a point 1.60m vertically from ground level, within 3m horizontal radius from the TSAL. - In direct sunlight.

docs.title: EV4.10.9
docs.text: The TSAL and all required circuitry must be hard-wired electronics. Software control is not permitted.

docs.title: EV4.10.10
docs.text: A green indicator light in the cockpit must illuminate if the TSAL green light is on, see EV4.10.3. It must be clearly marked “TS off”, and the light must be easily visible even in bright sunlight.

docs.title: EV4.10.11
docs.text: Signals influencing the TSAL and the indicator according to EV4.10.10 are SCS, see T11.9. The individual safe state of each of the TSAL lights is off. The TSAL has an active indication of the absence of failures (continuous green illumination) and thus the red light must not be illuminated for a visible check, see T11.9.6.

docs.title: EV4.10.12
docs.text: The TSAL’s red light voltage detection circuit, see EV4.10.2, does not need to detect an open circuit, as required by T11.9. A plausibility check must not be implemented.

docs.title: EV4.10.13
docs.text: Any implausibility in the circuit detecting the AIR and pre-charge relay states (see EV4.10.3) must result in the TSAL’s green light being extinguished. This is exempt from the requirement of T11.9.2.

docs.title: EV4.10.14
docs.text: Any implausibility between the AIR or pre-charge relay states and the expected voltage for these states (see EV4.10.3) must result in the TSAL’s green light being extinguished. This is exempt from the requirement of T11.9.2.

docs.title: EV4.10.15
docs.text: The latching required by EV4.10.13 and EV4.10.14 must not be triggered during normal operation conditions and must only be reset by power cycling the LVS.

docs.title: EV4.10.16
docs.text: The TSAL power supply must: - Comply with T11.7 and be capable of powering the TSAL for at least 15 minutes after the LVS has been switched off. It is permissible for the TSAL to be powered by the LVS whenever this is switched on. - Not be used to power any other systems, - Comply with all requirements of T11.1 but must not be de-activated by opening the LVMS (see T11.3).

docs.title: EV4.10.17
docs.text: It is permissible for the ESO to deactivate the TSAL when the LVS is switched off and if the TS is confirmed to be deactivated. - It must not be possible to activate the TS if the TSAL is in a deactivated state, - The driver must not be able to deactivate the TSAL.

docs.title: EV4.11.1
docs.text: The TS is active if any of the AIRs or the pre-charge relay are closed.

docs.title: EV4.11.2
docs.text: The driver must be able to activate and deactivate the TS from within the cockpit without the assistance of any other person.

docs.title: EV4.11.3
docs.text: [DV ONLY] The ASR must be able to activate the TS from outside the vehicle with an external TS activation button in proximity to the TSMS if and only if the ASMS is in “On” position.

docs.title: EV4.11.4
docs.text: Closing the shutdown circuit by any part defined in EV6.1.2 must not (re-)activate the TS. Additional action must be required.

docs.title: EV4.11.5
docs.text: [DV ONLY] The AS must not be able to (re-)activate the TS.

docs.title: EV4.11.6
docs.text: The vehicle is ready-to-drive as soon as the motor(s) will respond to the input of the APPS.

docs.title: EV4.11.7
docs.text: After the TS has been activated, additional actions must be required by the driver to set the vehicle to ready-to-drive mode (e.g. pressing a dedicated start button). The transition to ready-to-drive mode must only be possible during the actuation of the mechanical brakes and a simultaneous dedicated additional action.

docs.title: EV4.11.8
docs.text: The ready-to-drive mode must be left immediately when the shutdown circuit is opened.

docs.title: EV4.12.1
docs.text: The vehicle must make a characteristic sound, continuously for at least one second and a maximum of three seconds while entering ready-to-drive mode.

docs.title: EV4.12.2
docs.text: The sound level must be a minimum of 90dB(A), fast weighting. The sound level will be measured with a free-field microphone placed free from obstructions in a radius of 2m around the vehicle.

docs.title: EV4.12.3
docs.text: The sound must be easily recognisable. No animal voices, parts of songs or sounds that could be interpreted as offensive are permissible.

docs.title: EV4.12.4
docs.text: The vehicle must not make any other sounds similar to the ready-to-drive sound.

docs.title: EV5.1.1
docs.text: Cell – a battery cell or super-capacitor.

docs.title: EV5.1.2
docs.text: Cell Energy – the maximum cell voltage times the nominal capacity of the used cell.

docs.title: EV5.1.3
docs.text: TS Accumulator – all cells that store the electrical energy to be used by the TS as a whole.

docs.title: EV5.1.4
docs.text: Tractive System Accumulator Container (TSAC) – the container itself, which contains the TS accumulator.

docs.title: EV5.1.5
docs.text: TS Accumulator Segments – sub-divisions of the TS accumulator.

docs.title: EV5.2.1
docs.text: All types of cells except molten salt and thermal batteries are allowed.

docs.title: EV5.2.2
docs.text: Fuel cells are prohibited.

docs.title: EV5.3 Tractive System Energy Storage – General Requirements
EV5.3.1
docs.text: All cells that store the TS energy must be enclosed in a TSAC.

docs.title: EV5.3.2
docs.text: Each TS accumulator segment must not exceed: - a maximum voltage of 120 VDC, - a maximum energy of 6 MJ, see EV5.1.2, - a maximum mass of 12kg.

docs.title: EV5.3.3
docs.text: If spare TS accumulators are used, they must be of the same size, weight and type as those that are replaced.

docs.title: EV5.3.4
docs.text: Spare cells must be stored in an electrically insulated container made of fire-retardant material, see T1.2.1. The container must be labelled according to EV5.3.8.

docs.title: EV5.3.5
docs.text: Spare accumulators and spare cells should be presented at technical inspection.

docs.title: EV5.3.6
docs.text: It must be possible to open the TSAC for technical inspection.

docs.title: EV5.3.7
docs.text: Each TSAC must be removable from the vehicle while still remaining rules compliant without the need to install extra components. A dummy connector or similar may be used to restore the system’s isolation, see EV4.5.

docs.title: EV5.3.8
docs.text: The vehicle number, the university name and the ESO phone number(s) must be displayed and written in Roman Sans-Serif characters of at least 20mm high on the lid of each TSAC. The characters must be clearly visible and placed on a high contrast background.

docs.title: EV5.3.9
docs.text:
All TS Accumulators using chemistries other than lead acid must be: (a) Directly accessible with a fire extinguisher nozzle of 35mm diameter x 150mm long, without removing body panels and with the driver seated normally in the vehicle. Covers which can be easily "punched through" are acceptable.

Any such cover or access location must be identified using the appropriate symbol below and be clearly visible to marshals approaching the car.

Figure 27: Fire Port marking

If the TS Accumulator(s) is positioned greater than 50mm inboard of the access location, then a tube of at least 35mm diameter must be present to direct the discharge from the extinguisher towards the TS Accumulator(s). The tube must be no more than 750mm in length. Any access tube must be separated from the driver by a firewall as specified in T4.8. (b) Identified with the symbol below (minimum height 75mm and showing the appropriate battery chemistry) on each side of the car AND adjacent to any labels required by EV5.3.9(a).

Figure 28: Battery Chemistry marking

docs.title: EV5.4 Tractive System Energy Storage – Electrical Configuration
EV5.4.1
docs.text: Every TSAC must contain at least one fuse and at least two AIRs, see EV5.6 and EV3.2.7.

docs.title: EV5.4.2
docs.text: LVS must not be included in the TSAC except where inherently required. Exceptions include the AIRs, TS DC/DC converters, the Accumulator Management System (AMS), the Insulation Monitoring Device (IMD), parts of the TSAL and cooling fans.

docs.title: EV5.4.3
docs.text: Maintenance plugs must allow electrical separation of all TS accumulator segments, see EV5.3.2. The separation must affect both poles of all segments including first and last segment.

docs.title: EV5.4.4
docs.text: Maintenance plugs must: - Not require tools to separate the TS accumulator segments, - Be non-conductive on surfaces that do not provide any electrical connection, - Be designed in a way, that it is physically impossible to electrically connect them in any way other than the design intent configuration, - Be designed such that it is clearly visible whether the connection is open or closed. Electrically controlled switches must not be used.

docs.title: EV5.4.5
docs.text: Each TS accumulator segment must be electrically insulated by the use of suitable rigid and fire retardant, see T1.2.1, material between the segments and on top of the segment to prevent arc flashes caused by inter-segment contact or by parts/tools accidentally falling into the TSAC during maintenance.

docs.title: EV5.4.6
docs.text: Every wire used in an TSAC, regardless of whether it is part of the LVS or TS, must be follow EV4.5.2, EV4.5.3 and EV4.5.5.

docs.title: EV5.4.7
docs.text: Each TSAC must have a prominent indicator, a voltmeter or a red LED visible even in bright sunlight that will illuminate continuously whenever a voltage greater than 60 VDC or half the nominal TS voltage, whichever is lower, is present at the vehicle side of the AIRs.

docs.title: EV5.4.8
docs.text: The indicator must be clearly visible while disconnecting the TSAC from the vehicles. The indicator must be clearly marked with “Voltage Indicator”

docs.title: EV5.4.9
docs.text: The indicator must be hard-wired electronics without software control, directly and only supplied by the TS from the vehicle side of the AIRs, and always working, even if the accumulator is disconnected from the LVS or removed from the vehicle.

docs.title: EV5.5 Tractive System Energy Storage – Mechanical Configuration
EV5.5.1
docs.text: All TSACs must lie fully within, and be attached to, the Primary Structure, or any structure fixed to the Primary Structure, which meets the minimum specification for impact structures. In side view, the TSACs may not exceed the height of the impact structure, see T3.15.2.

docs.title: EV5.5.2
docs.text: All TSACs must be protected from impacts, see T3.15.2 and be no higher than their attendant impact structure. No part of the TSAC may be part of the primary structure.

docs.title: EV5.5.3
docs.text: All TSAC materials and mounts must be fire retardant, see T1.2.1. All calculations must be conducted for an ambient temperature of 60°C except for metallic materials and continuous fibre-reinforced laminates. Where materials are used within the TSAC which do not meet the requirements of T1.2.1 the team must be able to justify why they were used in preference to a fire-retardant material.

docs.title: EV5.5.4
docs.text: The design of the TSAC and its contents, calculations and/or tests must be documented in the SES. This includes materials used, drawings, images, fastener locations, segment weight, cell and segment position and any proof of equivalence.

docs.title: EV5.5.5
docs.text:
The TSAC(s) must be constructed of steel or aluminium. With the following requirements: - The floor of the TSAC must be at least 1.25mm thick if made from steel or 3.2mm if made from aluminium, - The internal and external vertical walls, covers and lids must be at least 0.9mm thick if made from steel or 2.3mm if made from aluminium.

Alternative materials are allowed with proof of equivalency per T3.3 or for composite materials per EV5.5.6. When alternative materials are used, test samples must be presented at technical inspection.

docs.title: EV5.5.6
docs.text: Composite TSAC(s) must satisfy the following requirements: - Data obtained from the laminate perimeter shear strength test and three point bending test, see T3.5, should be used to prove adequate strength is provided, - Each attachment point requires steel backing plates with a minimum thickness of 2mm. Alternate materials may be used for backing plates if equivalency is approved,

docs.title: EV5.5.7
docs.text: The floor and walls of the TSAC must be joined by welds, bonding and/or fasteners. - Fastened connections between the floor and any vertical wall of each section must have at least 2 fasteners, - Fastened connections between internal vertical walls and external vertical walls must be located in the top half of the internal vertical wall, - Sections containing 8kg or less must have a minimum of 2 fasteners connecting any two vertical walls, - Sections containing between 8kg and 12kg must have a minimum of 3 fasteners connecting any two vertical walls.

docs.title: EV5.5.8
docs.text:
The TSAC must include electrically insulating internal vertical walls with a minimum of 75% of the height of the external vertical walls, which divide the TSAC into section of a maximum of 12kg.

NOTE: This is less restrictive than the Formula Student Germany 2026 Rules, if you plan to compete at other events the internal walls must extend up to the lid.

docs.title: EV5.5.9
docs.text: The accumulator segments, see EV5.3.2, must be separated by a rigid, electrically insulating and fire-retardant barrier, see T1.2.1.

docs.title: EV5.5.10
docs.text:
The TSAC and the mounting of the TSAC to the chassis, each segment to the TSAC and each cell within a segment must be designed to withstand the accelerations according to T9.2.

All TSAC attachment points must follow EV5.5.16. TSAC(s) made of materials as stated in EV5.5.5 or EV5.5.6 may need further reinforcement in order to comply with this rule.

docs.title: EV5.5.11
docs.text: Tabs of pouch cells must not carry mechanical loads and must not press into the pouch. Pouch cells must only carry mechanical loads on the large surface areas. The load must be distributed over at least 80% of each surface carrying the load.

docs.title: EV5.5.12
docs.text: Friction based cell mounting requires physical testing to prove the cells are retained when subjected to the required loads. Mechanically representative test cells or mock-up cells are permissible for these tests.

docs.title: EV5.5.13
docs.text: To fulfil EV 5.5.10, a cell may be loaded with a maximum shear stress of 0.05MPa and a compressive stress of 1.0MPa. When calculating the stress, only 80% of the nominal large cell surface area may be used.

docs.title: EV5.5.14
docs.text: All fasteners used within or to mount the TSAC must comply with T10. Fasteners within the TSAC used for non-structural TSAC parts (e.g. PCBs etc.) do not have to follow T10 if the fasteners are made of electrically non-conductive material or other than stated in T10.1.2, may be of any diameter. Non-structural fasteners used to mount tabs of pouch cells must comply with T10 with the exception of T10.1.2.

docs.title: EV5.5.15
docs.text: The AIRs and the main fuse, see EV3.2.7, must be separated with an electrically insulated and fire-retardant material, see T1.2.1, from the cells within the TSAC (see EV5.1.3). Air is not considered to be a suitable insulation material in this case.

docs.title: EV5.5.16
docs.text: The TSAC must be attached to the chassis by a minimum of two mounts. Any brackets used to mount the TSAC must be made of steel 1.6mm thick or aluminium 4mm thick and must have gussets to carry bending loads.

docs.title: EV5.5.17
docs.text: Holes, both internal and external, in the TSAC are only allowed for the wiring-harness, ventilation, cooling or fasteners. Holes may extend to the edge of a wall. The TSAC must still be compliant with all other rules, especially the ones concerning its structural requirements. External holes must be sealed according to EV4.5. The total cutout area must be below 25% of the area of the respective single wall.

docs.title: EV5.5.18
docs.text: External openings for cooling and connected cooling ducts must not point towards the driver, or if the accumulator is out of the car, towards the operator of the accumulator hand cart even though there is a firewall, see T4.8, in between. Ducts and their mounting must be fire retardant, see T1.2.1, and properly sealed.

docs.title: EV5.5.19
docs.text: A sticker according to “ISO 7010-W012” (triangle with black lightning bolt on yellow background) with triangle side length of at least 100mm and the text “Always Energized” must be applied on every TSAC. The sticker must also contain the text “High Voltage” if the voltage is more than 60VDC or 25VAC.

docs.title: EV5.5.20
docs.text: Every TSAC must be able to vent gas to prevent high-pressure in the TSAC.

docs.title: EV5.5.21
docs.text: Where there are liquid cooling elements within the accumulator container, teams must demonstrate how they have been designed, manufactured and tested to ensure that cooling liquid cannot leak into the accumulator.

docs.title: EV5.6.1
docs.text: At least two AIRs must be fitted inside each TSAC.

docs.title: EV5.6.2
docs.text: The AIRs must open both poles of the TS accumulator. If the AIRs are open, no TS voltage may be present outside of the TSAC and the vehicle side of the AIRs must be galvanically isolated from the accumulator side, see EV1.2.1.

docs.title: EV5.6.3
docs.text: The AIRs must be mechanical relays of a “normally open” type. Solid-state relays are prohibited.

docs.title: EV5.7.1
docs.text: A circuit that ensures that the voltage at the vehicle side of the AIRs is pre-charged to at least 95 % of the actual TS accumulator voltage before closing the second AIR must be implemented. Therefore the intermediate circuit voltage must be measured.

docs.title: EV5.7.2
docs.text: The pre-charge circuit must use a mechanical, normally open type relay. All pre-charge current must pass through this relay.

docs.title: EV5.8.1
docs.text: Each TS accumulator must be monitored by an AMS whenever the LVS is active, or the accumulator is connected to a charger.

docs.title: EV5.8.2
docs.text: Every TSAC must contain its full AMS including its own and AMS exclusive SDC power stage, see EV 6.1

docs.title: EV5.8.3
docs.text: The AMS must continuously measure - All cell voltages, - The TS current, - The temperature of thermally critical cells, - For lithium-based cells: the temperature of at least 30 % of the cells equally distributed within the TSAC(s).

docs.title: EV5.8.4
docs.text:
Cell temperature must be measured at the negative terminal of the respective cell or at a location representative of the cell’s maximum temperature. The sensor used must be in direct contact with the electrically exposed negative terminal (or location representative of the cell’s maximum temperature) or less than 10mm along the high current path away from the terminal in direct contact with the respective busbar.

Where the sensor placement is not at the negative terminal (or less than 10mm along the high current path from it), the team must justify the placement in the ESF. The justification must quantify the measurement error, considering thermal resistance and cooling effects. For pouch cells the reference point for error evaluation is the point where the tab leaves pouch bag.

It is acceptable to monitor multiple cells with one sensor if the above requirements are met for all cells sensed by the sensor.

If thermal adhesive is used to ensure contact between the cell and temperature sensor, the maximum permitted temperature must be reduced, and the reduction justified in the ESF.

docs.title: EV5.8.5
docs.text: The maximum cell temperature is 60°C or the limit stated in the cell data sheet, whichever is lower.

docs.title: EV5.8.6
docs.text:
An independent cell temperature monitoring device may be provided by the officials during accumulator inspection and must be installed.

The device must be placed on the warmest negative cell terminal of the TSAC and in direct contact with the terminal or less then 30mm away from it on the busbar.

docs.title: EV5.8.7
docs.text:
The AMS must switch off the TS via the shutdown circuit, if critical voltage, temperature or current values according to the cell manufacturer’s datasheet or these rules persistently occurs for more than: - 500ms for voltage and current values, - 1s for temperature values.

The accuracy, noise and sample rate of the measurement must be taken into account.

docs.title: EV5.8.8
docs.text: AMS cell voltage measurement inputs, temperature measurement inputs and supply voltage of decentralized AMS slaves may be rated below the maximum TS voltage if the team can demonstrate that the chosen rating is appropriate for the situation.EV9

docs.title: EV5.8.9
docs.text: A red indicator light in the cockpit that is easily visible from inside and outside the cockpit even in bright sunlight and clearly marked with the lettering “AMS” must light up if the AMS opens the shutdown circuit. It must stay illuminated until the error state has been manually reset, see EV6.1.6. Signals controlling this indicator are SCS, see T11.9.

docs.title: EV5.8.10
docs.text: AMS signals are System Critical Signals, see T11.9. The loss of any measurement connection, see EV5.8.3, must result in an opened Shutdown Circuit.

docs.title: EV5.8.11
docs.text: It must be possible to individually disconnect the current sensor, one temperature sensor and one cell voltage measurement wire during technical inspection, if any wire used.

docs.title: EV5.8.12
docs.text: The AMS must be able to read and display all measured values according to EV5.8.2, including a single overview, e.g. by connecting a laptop to the AMS. This may be requested by officials anywhere, at any time, e.g. within a Dynamic Area.

docs.title: EV6.1.1
docs.text: The shutdown circuit directly carries the power driving the AIRs, see EV5.6, and the pre- charge circuitry, see EV5.7.

docs.title: EV6.1.2
docs.text:
The shutdown circuit is defined as a series connection of at least two master switches, three shutdown buttons, the BOTS, see T6.2, the IMD, the inertia switch, see T11.5, the BSPD, see T11.6, all required interlocks and the AMS.

An explanatory schematic of the required shutdown circuit, excluding any possible interlock circuitry, is shown in Figure 29.

Figure 29: Explanatory example schematic of the required shutdown circuit.

Elements marked ** are only required for ADS. Elements marked * are required in accordance with the associated rule(s).

docs.title: EV6.1.3
docs.text: All parts of the shutdown circuit defined in EV6.1.2 must be on the high-side connection of the AIR coils and the pre-charge circuitry.

docs.title: EV6.1.4
docs.text:
The Tractive System Master Switch (TSMS), see EV6.2, must be the last switch before the AIRs except for pre-charge circuitry and hardwired interlocks.

NOTE: Whilst hardwired interlocks may be located after the TSMS, it is good practice for them to be before the TSMS

docs.title: EV6.1.5
docs.text:
If the shutdown circuit is opened, the TS must be shutdown by opening all AIRs and the pre-charge relay. The voltage in the TS must drop to below 60VDC and 25VACRMS in less than five seconds. All TS accumulator current flow must stop immediately.

The action of opening the AIRs may be delayed by ≤250ms to signal the action to the motor controllers and reduce the TS current before the AIRs are opened. The AIR supply must be abruptly switched off before reaching the minimum AIR supply voltage.

docs.title: EV6.1.6
docs.text: If the shutdown circuit is opened by the AMS or the IMD, it has to be latched open by a non-programmable logic that can only be manually reset by a person at the vehicle who is not the driver.

docs.title: EV6.1.7
docs.text: All circuits that are part of the shutdown circuit must be designed in a way, that in the de- energized/disconnected state they open the shutdown circuit.

docs.title: EV6.1.8
docs.text: It must be possible to demonstrate that all features of the shutdown circuit function correctly. This includes all interlocks.

docs.title: EV6.1.9
docs.text: Every system that is required to or is able to open the shutdown circuit must have its own, non-programmable, power stage to achieve this. The respective power stages must be designed to be able to carry the shutdown circuit current, e.g. AIR inrush currents, and such that a failure cannot result in electrical power being fed back into the electrical shutdown circuit.

docs.title: EV6.1.10
docs.text: The shutdown buttons, the BOTS, the TSMS and all interlocks must not act through any power stage.

docs.title: EV6.1.11
docs.text: All signals influencing the shutdown circuit are SCSs, see T11.9.

docs.title: EV6.2.1
docs.text: An TSMS according to T11.2 must be part of the shutdown circuit, see EV6.1.2.

docs.title: EV6.2.2
docs.text: The TSMS must be fitted with a “lockout/tagout” capability to prevent accidental activation of the TS. The ESO must ensure that it is locked in the off position whenever work is done on the vehicle or no ESO is present.

docs.title: EV6.2.3
docs.text: The TSMS must be mounted in the middle of a completely orange circular area of ≥50mm diameter placed on a high contrast background.

docs.title: EV6.2.4
docs.text: The TSMS must be marked with “TS” and a symbol according to “ISO 7010-W012” (triangle with black lightning bolt on yellow background).

docs.title: EV6.3.1
docs.text: Every vehicle must have an IMD installed in the TS system.

docs.title: EV6.3.2
docs.text: The IMD must be a Bender A-ISOMETER® iso-F1 IR155-3203 or -3204, -4203, or -4204, or a Bender ISOMETER® iso165C-1, iso175, or equivalent IMD approved for automotive use. Equivalency may be approved by the officials based on the following criteria: robustness to vibration, operating temperature range, IP rating, availability of a direct output, a self- test facility and must not be powered by the system which is monitored.

docs.title: EV6.3.3
docs.text: The response value of the IMD must be set to ≥500 Ω/V, related to the maximum TS voltage.

docs.title: EV6.3.4
docs.text: The IMD response value must not be changed after electrical inspection.

docs.title: EV6.3.5
docs.text: The IMD must be connected on the vehicle side of the AIRs.

docs.title: EV6.3.6
docs.text: One IMD chassis ground measurement line must be connected to the grounded TSAC. The other chassis ground measurement line must be connected to the main hoop. Each connection must use a separate conductor, rated for at least maximum TS voltage. An open circuit in any of this ground measurement connections must result in an opened shutdown circuit.

docs.title: EV6.3.7
docs.text: In case of an insulation failure or an IMD failure, the IMD must open the shutdown circuit. This must be done without the influence of any programmable logic. See also EV6.1.6 regarding the re-activation of the TS after an insulation fault.

docs.title: EV6.3.8
docs.text: A red indicator light in the cockpit, that is easily visible from inside and outside the cockpit in bright sunlight and clearly marked with the lettering “IMD”, must light up if the IMD opens the shutdown circuit. It must stay illuminated until the error state has been manually reset, see EV6.1.6. Signals controlling this indicator are SCS, see T11.9.

docs.title: EV7.1.1
docs.text: Only chargers presented and sealed at technical inspection are allowed to be used. All connections of the charger(s) must be insulated and covered. No open connections are allowed.

docs.title: EV7.1.2
docs.text: Exposed conductive parts and the TSAC must be connected to protective earth (PE).

docs.title: EV7.1.3
docs.text: All chargers must either be accredited to a recognized standard e.g. CE, or when built by the team, must comply with all electrical requirements for the vehicle TS, e.g. EV4.3, EV3.1 and EV4.2.

docs.title: EV7.1.4
docs.text: TS charging leads must be orange.

docs.title: EV7.1.5
docs.text: When charging, the AMS must be live and must be able to turn off the charger and open the SDC, see EV7.2, in the event that a fault is detected.

docs.title: EV7.1.6
docs.text: The charger must include a push type emergency stop button which has a minimum diameter of 24mm and must be clearly labelled.

docs.title: EV7.1.7
docs.text: When charging the accumulator, an IMD as described in EV6.3 must be active and must be able to shut down the charger and open the SDC, see EV7.2. The second chassis ground measurement line must be connected to the casing of the charger.

docs.title: EV7.1.8
docs.text: An IMD indicator light as defined in EV6.3.8 must be available during charging.

docs.title: EV7.1.9
docs.text: An easily visible green indicator with the same functionality as the TSAL’s green light, see EV4.10.3, must be available.

docs.title: EV7.1.10
docs.text: The charger must include TSMPs as described in EV4.7. Other than stated, the TSMPs must be connected to the TS output of the charger.

docs.title: EV7.1.11
docs.text: All indicators, switches, buttons, and connectors of the charger must be labelled.

docs.title: EV7.2.1
docs.text: When charging, the charging shutdown circuit consists of at least the charger shutdown button, see EV7.1.6, the IMD, the AMS , and the charging leads’ interlocks.

docs.title: EV7.2.2
docs.text: If the shutdown circuit is opened the charging system must remain disabled and the shutdown circuit opened until it is manually reset. Closing the SDC by any part defined in EV7.2.1 must not (re-)activate charging.

docs.title: EV7.2.3
docs.text: The charging shutdown systems must comply with EV6.1.1, EV6.1.5, EV6.1.7, EV6.1.8 and EV6.1.9.

docs.title: EV7.2.4
docs.text: All signals influencing the charger shutdown circuit are SCS, see T11.9.

docs.title: Tractive System Accumulator Container Hand Cart
EV8.1 Tractive System Accumulator Container Hand Cart
EV8.1.1
docs.text: A hand cart(s) must be used for transporting the TSAC(s) around the competition site.

docs.title: EV8.1.2
docs.text: The hand cart(s) must have at least four wheels.

docs.title: EV8.1.3
docs.text: The hand cart(s) must have a brake that is normally on and only released if someone pushes the handle, or similar.

docs.title: EV8.1.4
docs.text: The brake must be capable of safely stopping the fully loaded hand cart.

docs.title: EV8.1.5
docs.text: The cart must be easy to move when the brake is released.

docs.title: EV8.1.6
docs.text: The hand cart(s) must be able to carry the load of the TSAC(s).

docs.title: EV8.1.7
docs.text: The hand cart must provide a vertical firewall (see T4.8) to protect anyone moving the hand cart. The firewall must be the same width as the hand cart, must appropriately protect the operator’s legs and body and be at least 30 cm higher than the hand cart handle and the TSAC. Any part of the firewall more than 1.3m above the ground must be transparent.

docs.title: EV8.1.8
docs.text: The TSAC(s) must be mechanically fixed to the hand cart(s) to enable safe transportation.

docs.title: EV8.1.9
docs.text: The TSAC(s) must not protrude outside the edges of the hand cart.

docs.title: EV8.1.10
docs.text: The TSAC(s) must be protected from vibrations and shocks during normal operation of the cart(s), e.g. by using pneumatic tyres.

docs.title: EV8.1.11
docs.text: The hand cart must have a label according to EV5.3.8 on its firewall no more than 1.3m above the ground. The label must be clearly visible when the TSAC is on the hand cart.

docs.title: EV8.1.12
docs.text: The overall floor space used by the fully loaded hand cart must not exceed 1200mm x 800mm. If the TSAC is larger than the allowed floor space, exceptions may be approved by the officials prior to the competition.

docs.title: EV9.1.1
docs.text: Prior to the competition, all teams must submit clearly structured documentation of their entire electrical system (including control and TS) called the ESF.

docs.title: EV9.1.2
docs.text: The ESF must follow the template provided on the Formula Student website, must not exceed one hundred and ten (110) pages and be submitted in pdf format. Submissions that do not meet these requirements may be rejected by the judges and considered as a non-submission.

docs.title: EV9.1.3
docs.text: Datasheet values and manufacturer recommendations must be adhered to for all items in the ESF, unless prior permission is sought and approved by submitting a rules question to the Formula Student Question Database.

docs.title: IN1.1.1
docs.text:
The technical inspection is divided into the following parts:

  • Motorsport UK Safety Inspection (SAFETY)
  • Mechanical Inspection (CHASSIS and TECH)
  • [EV Only] Accumulator Inspection (EV BATTERY)
  • [EV Only] Electrical Inspection (EV VEHICLE)
  • [EV Only] Rain Test
  • Noise Test (NOISE)
  • Tilt Test (TILT)
  • Brake Test (BRAKE)
  • Vehicle Weighing
  • Driver Egress Tests
  • [DV Only] Driverless Inspection
  • [DV Only] EBS Test

docs.title: IN1.2.1
docs.text: Each vehicle must pass all parts of technical inspection before it may participate in any dynamic event.

docs.title: IN1.2.2
docs.text: Passing the technical inspections is not a certification of complete rules compliance of the vehicle.

docs.title: IN1.2.3
docs.text: The technical inspection sheet includes several inspection points and will be provided on the competition website prior to the competition. It must always stay with the vehicle.

docs.title: IN1.2.4
docs.text: The officials may inspect other points not mentioned on the technical inspection sheet to ensure compliance with the rules.

docs.title: IN1.2.5
docs.text: Teams are responsible for confirming that their vehicle and the required equipment satisfies the requirements and restrictions of the rules before presenting it for technical inspection.

docs.title: IN1.2.6
docs.text: Vehicles must be presented for technical inspection in ready-to-race condition.

docs.title: IN1.2.7
docs.text: All items on the inspection sheet must be clearly visible for the officials without using instruments such as endoscopes or mirrors. Visible access may be provided by removing body panels or by providing removable access panels.

docs.title: IN1.2.8
docs.text: The vehicle must maintain all required specifications throughout the competition.

docs.title: IN1.2.9
docs.text: Officials reserve the right to ask the team for drilling of additional inspection holes to check the chassis for compliance with the rules.

docs.title: IN1.2.10
docs.text: Officials will mark or seal various different approved parts. Removal of or damage to the seals will void the inspection approval.

docs.title: IN1.2.11
docs.text: Once the vehicle is approved for competition, any damage to the vehicle that requires repair(s) will void the inspection approval. After completion of the repair(s), the vehicle must be re-submitted to technical inspection for re-approval.

docs.title: IN1.2.12
docs.text: The officials reserve the right to prohibit the use of parts that could pose a safety risk to drivers, track marshals or the environment.

docs.title: IN1.2.13
docs.text: The event organisers reserve the right to re-inspect the vehicle at any time during the event after passing technical inspection. If any non-compliances are identified, then the team may be disqualified from the run in the dynamic event that immediately preceded the re- inspection.

docs.title: IN1.3.1
docs.text: Technical inspection stickers will be placed on the upper nose of the vehicle.
